cards.subject: The aqir
lines: Long before the qiraji there were the aqir, who built temple cities and lost an empire, twice — once to the titan-forged and once to the trolls — and scattered.
The ones who stayed here were warped by what is under this building into something else. The temple is a monument to gods nobody is supposed to name, and a breeding ground for an army.

cards.subject: Worked stone, then a nest, then nothing
lines: The Temple is three distinct places and the difficulty follows the descent.
The wiki's own line: the first bosses match the hardest of Molten Core, and the last are harder than anything in Blackwing Lair.
It ends in a bare chamber with an eye in it.

cards.subject: The first boss is the priest
lines: Not a soldier. The religious leader of Ahn'Qiraj, and the man who wrote the Prophecy of C'Thun.
He splits into images of himself and teleports between three platforms.
"PREPARE... for the return of the ancient ones!"

cards.subject: Only the number of hits counts
lines: How hard the frost hits is irrelevant. Ten hits slow him, fifteen freeze him up, twenty freeze him solid.
So raids spammed the weakest, fastest frost spell they owned.
Then everyone with a weapon beat the ice statue until it exploded.

cards.subject: One takes no weapons, one takes no spells
lines: Damage to either hurts the other, so the raid splits in half and works on opposite brothers.
Keep them apart or they heal one another for thirty thousand a tick.
Every half-minute they teleport into each other's places and wipe all threat.

cards.subject: The longest-unkilled boss in vanilla
lines: The sandworm shipped so bugged, and was so easy to walk past, that the wiki records him standing eighty-six days after the world's first Twin Emperors kill.
The lore calls him something C'Thun made "as a mockery of life".
He spends most of the fight underground.

cards.subject: Phase one is only the eye
lines: The first half of the fight is a single enormous eyeball. The body it belongs to does not rise until the eye is dead.
Its beam chains to anyone standing within about ten yards and grows as it jumps.
Forty people standing far apart in a black room, being looked at.

cards.subject: It turns
lines: A red beam sweeps a hundred and eighty degrees through the room, once every eighty-five seconds, and kills anything at level sixty that it crosses.
You survive it by running the wall, staying behind the sweep.
There is nowhere in the chamber to hide from an eye.

cards.subject: You get eaten, and that is the plan
lines: His shell absorbs almost everything, so the only way through is from inside. Every ten seconds he swallows somebody.
Down there are two tentacles that have to die to drop the shell for forty-five seconds.
The raid wins by sending people to be digested on purpose.

cards.subject: For four months nobody could kill him
lines: C'Thun shipped and the raiding world could not do it — the second phase was widely held to be mathematically impossible with the gear of the day.
He was quietly hotfixed over months rather than in any patch.
Nihilum killed him on the twenty-fifth of April, hours after the last change.

cards.subject: You are riding something the building grew
lines: They drop off the trash and teach a silithid battle tank that may only be summoned inside this Temple, and that vanishes the instant you enter combat.
The crystal "emits a high frequency sound, forcing a silithid tank to burrow out from its home beneath the Temple."

cards.subject: You can mine the temple
lines: "The Statues in Ahn'Qiraj now drop chunks of obsidian that can be crafted by blacksmiths into various types of armor."
The building's own idols became a reagent.
You strip the temple for parts and then wear it.

cards.subject: The armour is a reputation grind
lines: Tokens off the bosses in here, and then standing with the bronze dragonflight on top.
Which is why these sets have names — Conqueror's Battlegear, Doomcaller's Attire, Garments of the Oracle — instead of a tier number.
